title: Design a 3.3V Voltage Divider
description: Convert a 5.0V source down to exactly 3.3V (+/-5%) using a two-resistor divider network to safely power 3.3V logic.
theoryExplanation: Using the voltage divider formula Vout = Vin * (R2 / (R1 + R2)), when Vin = 5.0V, selecting R1 = 1.8kOhm and R2 = 3.3kOhm yields Vout = 5.0 * (3.3 / 5.1) = 3.235V, well within the 3.3V logic threshold.

objectives.description: Measure an output voltage between 3.15V and 3.45V at the midpoint node.
Keep total quiescent current below 10 mA.

hints: Remember the divider formula: Vout = Vin * (R2 / (R1 + R2)).
Try standard resistor values: R1 = 1.8kOhm (or 1.7kOhm) and R2 = 3.3kOhm.
Connect a Multimeter in voltage mode across R2 and start the simulation.

title: Current-Limiting Resistor for LED
description: Calculate and insert the correct series resistor to safely drive a red LED from a 5V supply at 15-20mA without burning out the diode.
theoryExplanation: With forward voltage Vf approx 2.0V and target current If = 20mA (0.02A), Ohm's Law gives R = (Vin - Vf) / If = (5.0 - 2.0) / 0.02 = 150Ohm to 220Ohm.

objectives.description: The LED is successfully powered and illuminated.
Branch current through LED is between 12mA and 25mA.

hints: Use Ohm's Law: R = (Vsupply - Vled) / Iled.
For a standard red LED: Vf approx 2.0V, so resistor drops 3.0V.
A 150Ohm to 220Ohm resistor will provide the ideal 15-20mA current.

title: 8-Bit Serial Expander with 74HC595
description: Drive a 74HC595 shift register using SER (Data), SRCLK (Shift Clock), and RCLK (Latch Clock) to light up an 8-bit binary pattern.
theoryExplanation: The 74HC595 contains an internal 8-bit shift register and an 8-bit storage register. Pulsing SRCLK shifts data bit-by-bit; pulsing RCLK latches all 8 bits simultaneously onto parallel outputs QA-QH.

objectives.description: 74HC595 output register contains non-zero shifted data.
At least 3 LEDs connected to parallel outputs are actively lit.

hints: Connect Arduino D2 to SER (Data), D3 to SRCLK (Shift Clock), and D4 to RCLK (Latch).
Use `shiftOut(dataPin, clockPin, MSBFIRST, 0b10101010);` in Arduino code.
Toggle the latch pin LOW before shiftOut and HIGH after to latch outputs.

title: 1 kHz Square Wave Generator (NE555)
description: Configure an NE555 timer in astable multivibrator mode to generate a continuous 1.0 kHz (+/-10%) square wave output.
theoryExplanation: In astable mode, oscillation frequency f = 1.44 / ((R1 + 2*R2) * C1). Selecting C1 = 100nF (0.1uF), R1 = 1kOhm, R2 = 6.8kOhm produces f approx 1.44 / ((1000 + 13600) * 1e-7) approx 986 Hz, close to 1 kHz.

objectives.description: Oscilloscope detects oscillating output frequency of 1000 Hz +/- 100 Hz.

hints: Connect R1 between VCC and Pin 7 (DISCH), and R2 between Pin 7 and Pin 6/2.
Connect timing capacitor C1 between Pin 6/2 and GND.
